stem: What is the greatest number of bags of seed the team can buy?
stimulus: An agronomy team has a $1,400 grant for a field trial. It will spend $260 on soil testing and $38 for each bag of seed. The team must leave at least $90 of the grant unspent.
explanation: Write the spending as $260 + 38b$. Leaving at least $90 unspent means spending is at most $90 less than $1,400, so $260 + 38b \le 1400 - 90 = 1310$. Subtract 260 to get $38b \le 1050$, so $b \le 27.6...$. The team can only buy whole bags, so the greatest number is 27. Buying 28 bags would cost $260 + 1064 = 1324$ dollars, which is more than the $1,310 allowed.

common_errors.why: Ignored the $90 that must stay unspent and solved $260 + 38b \le 1400$, getting $b \le 30$.
Rounded 27.6 up. 28 bags costs $1,324, which goes over the $1,310 limit.
Dropped the $260 testing fee and solved $38b \le 1310$, getting $b \le 34.5$.

stem: What is the greatest possible number of the lowest-numbered unit?
stimulus: Along the north wall of a dig site, excavation units are numbered with consecutive odd integers. A crew is assigned three consecutive units whose numbers have a sum of at most 200.
explanation: Call the lowest number $n$. Consecutive odd integers are 2 apart, so the other two units are $n + 2$ and $n + 4$. 'At most' means ≤, so $n + (n+2) + (n+4) \le 200$, which gives $3n + 6 \le 200$. Then $3n \le 194$, so $n \le 64.67$. The number $n$ must be odd, so the greatest value is 63. Check: $63 + 65 + 67 = 195$, which works, and $65 + 67 + 69 = 201$, which is too big.

common_errors.why: Used $n+1$ and $n+2$ as the next two odd integers, so $3n + 3 \le 200$ and $n \le 65.67$. That gives 65.
Solved $n \le 64.67$ correctly, then took the greatest integer and forgot that the number must be odd.
Stopped at $3n \le 194$ and gave the right-hand side as the answer.

stem: What is the shortest length, in centimeters, at which the trail can be drawn on the map?
stimulus: On a park map, 1 centimeter represents 4 kilometers. The actual length of a planned trail must be no less than 10 kilometers less than the 82-kilometer length of the park's river.
explanation: If the trail is $x$ cm long on the map, its actual length is $4x$ km. 'No less than' means ≥. '10 less than 82' means $82 - 10$. So $4x \ge 82 - 10 = 72$, and $x \ge 18$. The shortest map length is 18 cm.

Found the shortest actual length in kilometers and never converted it to map centimeters.
Ignored the '10 kilometers less than' and solved $4x \ge 82$.
